subject: Re: Greengrid security questionnaire – data minimization, TTL & deletion flow
messages:
From: Elaine Hart <elaine.hart@greengrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greengrid Security <security@greengrid.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Nov 2024 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data retention/TTL questions for Hosted API

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security team asked a few specific follow-ups about how Redwood handles customer data in the Hosted API, especially around data minimization and deletion: 

1) Can customers set a TTL on stored request/response logs per-project or per-API-key? 
2) What is the default retention for full logs, and is there a separate window for metrics/telemetry? 
3) How are backups handled—are they included in the same deletion window or retained longer?
4) If a customer requests a full purge (subject access / erasure), what is the end-to-end timeline and what evidence do you provide?

We'd appreciate concise answers we can paste into our questionnaire. If you have a short diagram or matrix, please attach.

Best,
Elaine Hart
Head of Security Operations
Greengrid, Inc.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Hart <elaine.hart@greengrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Nov 2024 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data retention/TTL questions for Hosted API

Hi Elaine — thanks for the great questions. High-level answers below; cc'ing Ben for the infra/backup details and Stephanie for legal/compliance artifacts. I'll attach a simple TTL matrix and a diagram that map to each bullet.

1) Customer-configurable TTLs: yes. Customers may set per-API-key or per-project retention policies via the Console or our Management API. Options: ephemeral (0 days), short (7/30 days), medium (90 days), long (365 days), or custom N days. Default for newly created projects is 90 days for full request/response logs.

2) Default vs. telemetry: full request+response logs (payloads + metadata) default to 90 days. Aggregated metrics/telemetry (usage counts, latency histograms) are retained 365 days by default but can be reduced to 90 days for privacy-sensitive customers. Aggregates do not contain user-level prompt text.

3) Backups: backups are incremental and encrypted at rest; they are rolled forward and retained for 14 days for disaster recovery by default. Backups do not extend customer retention windows for deletion requests—we run a coordinated purge job that removes data from primary stores and prunes within backup windows, with verification steps. See Ben's note for the technical deletion flow.

4) Erasure workflow & timeline: standard customer-initiated purge is completed within 72 hours from request acceptance (confirmation + authentication). For legal holds or complex exports, the window may be extended and documented. After purge completes we provide an erasure confirmation report (timestamped, includes object IDs and worker run IDs). For compliance-heavy customers we can provide signed reports and audit logs via our Compliance Console.

We also provide options for real-time redaction (masking PII at the SDK level) and prefix/KV caching exclusions so sensitive prefixes never persist in logs.

Ben — can you add the deletion verification details and the backup-pruning schedule? Stephanie — I can loop compliance artifacts and SOC2 references once Ben confirms.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Elaine Hart <elaine.hart@greengrid.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 06 Nov 2024 10:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data retention/TTL questions for Hosted API

Thanks — technical details below. Attached a concise dataflow diagram and a retention matrix.

Deletion and verification flow (hosted API):
- Acceptance & auth: we validate the requestor via account owner credentials + MFA.
- Quiesce + snapshot: we pause write pipelines for the affected project and take a short-lived tombstone snapshot to enumerate affected objects.
- Primary purge: background workers remove objects from hot stores (KV caches, blobstore, index shards). This is typically completed within minutes for small footprints; larger datasets are batched.
- Backup pruning: our backup retention window is 14 days; once primary purge completes we tag backups for expedited pruning. Physical removal from backups occurs within the backup window (up to 14 days).
- Verification: once pruning is complete, we run read-after-delete checks and index scans to ensure no residual keys. The process emits a run ID and a SHA256 hash summary of deleted object IDs; these are included in the erasure confirmation.

Notes on snapshots & legal holds: if a legal hold is active we flag the tombstone snapshot and do not prune until the hold is released. Holds are a manual process requested through Compliance and logged in JIRA-SEC with owner and expiry.

Encryption & key management: all customer data at rest is encrypted with per-tenant keys in our KMS. When keys are rotated or destroyed per-customer, we follow NIST guidance and maintain an auditable key lifecycle in the Compliance Console.

Logging & telemetry separation: request payloads are stored encrypted and only accessible via a service ACL. Aggregated telemetry is emitted to a separate analytics cluster with different retention and no raw prompt text.

If you need a tighter backup window (e.g., backups pruned same day), we can offer that under a Dedicated contract or as a Private deployment option.

Ben Carter
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Greengrid Security <security@greengrid.com>

Marissa / Ben — this is exactly what we needed, thank you. A couple quick clarifications so we can close our questionnaire: 

• For the erasure confirmation, can you confirm the report contains the run ID, timestamp, list of object IDs (or hashed IDs) and the verification SHA256 summary?
• When a customer sets a custom TTL shorter than the backup window (for example, 1 day), do you still honor the primary purge and then prune backups on the 14-day schedule, or do you offer an accelerated backup prune for Hosted customers?

If you can confirm those two items I'll include the text in our questionnaire. Also please attach any compliance artifacts (SOC2 section references or Audit Report IDs) that we can provide to our procurement team.

Best,
Elaine
